name: @braice/api
//engines: Matches the root package.json and the Dockerfile's node:24 base, and is what Vercel reads when the project Root Directory is apps/api. Stated here as well so the function runtime does not silently drift from the version the image is built on.

scripts.//prebuild: The three workspace dependencies resolve through node_modules symlinks to their `types`, which points at dist/. Nothing here can see their sources: tsconfig.json sets rootDir to ./src, so mapping the paths at packages/*/src instead would fail the emit with TS6059. The dependencies therefore have to be BUILT first, and this script is what guarantees that, because `nest build` on its own is not enough. Anything that runs this package's build directly - `pnpm --filter @braice/api build`, or Vercel's NestJS framework preset, which runs bare `nest build` - otherwise fails with 36 errors of TS2307 'Cannot find module @braice/permission-engine', followed by TS7006 downstream wherever a type from one of those packages was inferring a parameter. The selector `@braice/api^...` is the dependencies WITHOUT this package, so it cannot recurse back into here. pnpm runs dependencies in topological order, so governance-engine and types are built before the packages that import them.
